title: Contentment
hook: I have learned to be content
tomorrow: Pop's surgery runs long. what does love do in a waiting room?

segments.voice: Yesterday a crowd went from tears to a feast and found that joy is strength. Today, a thank-you note from a man in chains.
screen: `JOY IS STRENGTH.` → `NOW, A NOTE FROM PRISON.`

segments.voice: A gym shirt, a team banner, a phone wallpaper: I can do all things through Christ. It reads like a promise to win. It comes from a thank-you note written in bonds. Paul is a prisoner, his letter to the Philippians says, and friends have sent him a gift. He thanks them, then adds that he isn't saying it because he's in need: “I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.” So which is it: a line for winning, or a line for doing without?
screen: `ON A GYM SHIRT.` → `FROM A PRISON LETTER.` → `WINNING, OR DOING WITHOUT?`

segments.voice: Read the lines around it first: “I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.” Then: “I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.” Christians read that sentence two ways. The first hears all things widely. Christ strengthens a person for whatever they're truly called to: a hard exam, a new city, a final with everything on the line. Paul didn't fence the words in, and a believer facing something big is right to lean on that strength. The second reading stays inside the paragraph. All things means hunger and plenty, prison and freedom. It's a sentence about endurance more than achievement: the strength to stay the same person whether the cupboard is full or empty. Paul names that setting himself, and he says he learned it, the way someone learns a trade. Both readings agree on the hinge: the strength comes through Christ, not from the shirt. And the letter to the Hebrews gives contentment its floor: “be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.” Contentment rests on company, not on stuff.
screen: `FULL AND HUNGRY ALIKE.` · `VIEW ONE: STRENGTH FOR ANY CALLING.` · `VIEW TWO: STRENGTH TO ENDURE.` · `I WILL NEVER LEAVE THEE.` · then, large: `CONTENT.`

segments.voice: Look at one thing you already own that still does its job: a mug, an old pair of shoes, a phone with a cracked corner. Keep your eyes on it and let it be enough for today. If you pray, you can hold Paul's words: I have learned to be content.
Contentment. Being steady whether there's plenty or little: learned over time, and resting on God's company.
Keep this one: content, learned slowly, in plenty and in need. Day seventeen thirty-nine, done.

screen: `DAY 1739 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 58 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DOES LOVE DO IN A WAITING ROOM?`

howItsDone: Christians cultivate contentment through practices such as fasting, simple living and giving, and through prayer; some read Philippians 4:11–13 and Hebrews 13:5 together on the subject.

fork.setup: your teammate says Philippians 4:13 is about hunger and plenty, not winning games. state the other view at its strongest.
options: Paul didn't fence in 'all things'; Christ can strengthen a person for any real calling.
say the verse before a game and a win is guaranteed.

fork.reveal: view one's best case: the words are wide, and the strength is Christ's. view two answers that Paul names the setting himself: full and hungry. both say the strength comes through Christ.

what it means: staying steady with plenty or little, learned like a trade.

guess: staying steady whether you have plenty or little
settling for less and giving up on hope
feeling satisfied once you own enough things
recall: a gladness given that holds you up

chat.says: nia got a whole new dorm set. i got my cousin's old sheets. trying not to be jealous
options: Paul learned to be content with plenty or little. Old sheets still work; steady is the gift.
Say 'I can do all things through Christ' and trust a new set is on its way.
Contentment means never wanting anything better, so being jealous is a fail.
chat.meaning: Paul's 'all things' includes being full and being hungry. He learned contentment in plenty and in need, resting on God's company, not on stuff.
